stories.headline: Trump rushed off stage after shots fired at White House Correspondents’ Dinner President Donald Trump was swiftly escorted off the stage by Secret Service after possible shots were fired at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in Washing
stories.summary: President Donald Trump was swiftly escorted off the stage by Secret Service at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, DC, after possible shots were fired. The incident occurred on Saturday during the annual event hosted by the White House reporters' association. Trump reported that a Secret Service agent was shot at but saved by his bulletproof vest. The FBI confirmed that a suspect was taken into custody. The White House Correspondents' Dinner is typically a lighthearted event featuring comedy and a satirical speech from the president. The sudden interruption by the shooting incident led to Trump's rapid removal from the stage, ensuring his safety. The investigation into the incident is ongoing, with the suspect currently in custody.

stories.headline: Egypt seeks to isolate Ethiopia with diplomacy blitz in Africa as nations quarrel over water - The National 01:00 Egypt seeks to isolate Ethiopia with diplomacy blitz in Africa as nations quarrel over water Cairo broadens Horn of Africa campaign of collaboration to other pa
stories.summary: Egypt is engaging in a diplomatic drive to rally support from other African nations in its water dispute with Ethiopia. The dispute centers around Ethiopia's management of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), which Egypt claims causes "significant harm" to downstream nations. Egypt's President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has issued warnings to Ethiopia, accusing it of unilateral actions without reaching agreements with downstream countries. Egypt is broadening its collaboration efforts in the Horn of Africa to counter Ethiopia's influence and growing Israeli presence in the continent. The move includes military cooperation agreements, diplomatic alliances, and regional engagement initiatives to regain leverage in the changing hydropolitical environment surrounding the Nile Basin. Egypt's efforts aim to isolate Ethiopia and protect its interests in the region.

stories.headline: China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi tells Myanmar leader Beijing will back its security, sovereignty China is also willing to cooperate with Myanmar to eradicate the scourge of telecommunications fraud.
stories.summary: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw, pledging Beijing's support for Myanmar's national sovereignty and security. Wang stated that China will "firmly support" Myanmar in safeguarding its security and sovereignty. Additionally, China is willing to cooperate with Myanmar to eradicate online gambling and telecommunications fraud, which has become a significant issue in the country. Myanmar has emerged as a hotspot for cyberscam operations in recent years. China also expressed its support for Myanmar's participation in regional dialogue and cooperation mechanisms, including enhanced interaction with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). The meeting aimed to strengthen bilateral ties and cooperation between China and Myanmar, with China offering to help Myanmar engage more with multilateral platforms.

stories.headline: Taiwan foreign minister arrives in Eswatini after president's trip blocked TAIPEI - Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung arrived in Eswatini saying Taipei would not be held back by "authoritarian forces", after the government accused
stories.summary: Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung arrived in Eswatini, stating that Taipei will not be held back by "authoritarian forces". The visit comes after a planned presidential trip to the African nation was abruptly cancelled, with Taiwan accusing China of exerting pressure behind the scenes. Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te was scheduled to visit Eswatini, but the trip was blocked. Since taking office, Lin Chia-lung has sought to consolidate a diplomatic vision that promotes Taiwan's allies' security and prosperity. The move is seen as a challenge to China's influence, as Taiwan's sovereignty is threatened by foreign military threats. The US has finalized a new arms sale with Taiwan, further straining relations with China, which claims the island as its own. Lin's visit to Eswatini is a demonstration of Taiwan's commitment to its diplomatic relationships despite external pressure.

stories.headline: Xbox Game Pass Officially Adds 15 New Free Games Available Day One
stories.summary: Xbox Game Pass has officially added 15 new free games, available to play on the day of their launch. Subscribers to Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC will have access to over a dozen new games for free throughout the rest of 2026. The new additions include Xbox published games and third-party titles, as well as Fortnite Crew, EA Play, and Ubisoft+ Classics. Meanwhile, 9 games will be leaving Game Pass in April 2026. The new releases are highly anticipated, with one game already being hailed as 'Absolute Peak' and a potential Game of the Year contender. Xbox Game Pass subscribers will have access to some of the year's most nominated games, making it a key service for gamers. The additions are part of the service's ongoing efforts to provide new content to its subscribers.

stories.headline: Google might be doing away with the Fitbit brand
stories.summary: Google is reportedly planning to phase out the Fitbit brand, at least on the software side. The company may rename Fitbit services to Google Health, as indicated by recent appearances of "Google Health Premium" in international Google Store listings. New imagery suggests the iconic Fitbit branding might be replaced with Google-centered branding. However, the Fitbit brand may still be used for hardware, such as the upcoming Google Fitbit Air display-less fitness tracker. The Fitbit mobile app may also be rebranded as "Google Health," based on recent icon changes. The move comes as Fitbit approaches its 20th birthday, and Google continues to integrate the brand it acquired in 2019. The changes are expected to occur on the software and services side, while the Fitbit brand may still be used for physical products.

stories.headline: realme 16 Series 5G hits PH market, offers 200MP cameras, 7,000mAh battery
stories.summary: The realme 16 Series 5G has been officially launched in the Philippines, featuring enhanced photography capabilities with 200MP cameras, extended battery life with 7,000mAh batteries, and advanced AI features. The series includes three models, all of which boast AMOLED displays and IP69 durability. Prices for the realme 16 Series 5G start at Php 25,999. The launch is accompanied by promo offers and freebies. The new lineup is designed to provide users with a comprehensive smartphone experience, combining high-quality cameras, long-lasting batteries, and intelligent AI tools. The realme 16 Series 5G is now available in the Philippine market, offering consumers a range of options to suit their needs and preferences. The series includes the realme 16, realme 16 Pro, and realme 16 Pro Plus models.

stories.headline: Microsoft drops Copilot branding in Notepad for Windows 11 for everyone, but it’s really just a rename
stories.summary: Microsoft has removed the Copilot branding from Notepad in Windows 11, replacing the Copilot icon with a pen icon and renaming the AI menu to "writing tools." This change is available in the latest Windows Insider preview build, 11.2512.28.0, which is now accessible to all Windows Insiders. The AI-powered features remain fully functional and are now managed under "Advanced features." This rename is part of a broader effort by Microsoft to reduce the visibility of Copilot branding in Windows 11 apps, including Notepad and Snipping Tool. While the entry points for these features have been reduced, the underlying AI capabilities remain intact, indicating a rebranding rather than a removal of the technology. The update aims to simplify the user interface and streamline access to AI-powered tools.

stories.headline: ‘Appalling’: Shattered Storm duo without answers in jarring vision as ugly stat comes to light
stories.summary: A winter storm has resulted in the deaths of 42 people, with a mother-daughter duo among the victims. The duo went missing after losing contact with a person they were talking to on the phone. Sheriff Tony Robinson confirmed their deaths, with officials investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. The storm had prompted warnings of "significant and extended power outages" from Spanberger, with state police and the National Guard deployed to assist with debris removal and other needs. The incident has highlighted the severity of the storm, which has left many without answers or resolution. The mother-daughter duo's deaths have been particularly jarring, with officials working to provide support to those affected by the storm. The full extent of the damage and loss of life is still being assessed.

stories.headline: Celtics Get Surprising Good News on Jaylen Brown Injury Before Game 4
stories.summary: Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown has received a positive update on his injury, boosting the team's hopes before Game 4. Brown, who averaged 22.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 4.5 assists in 63 regular season appearances, had been ruled out for the last two games. However, he participated fully in practice, according to coach Joe Mazzulla. Team insider Jay King reported that Brown's involvement in practice is a good sign for his availability in the upcoming game. Brown's potential return would be a significant boost to the Celtics, given his impressive performance in the regular season, which earned him his fourth All-Star Game appearance. The update on Brown's injury is a welcome surprise for the team, and his return could have a significant impact on their chances in Game 4. Brown's participation in practice suggests he may be ready to play.

stories.headline: Ottawa Senators swept out of NHL playoffs by Carolina Hurricanes
stories.summary: The Ottawa Senators have been swept out of the Stanley Cup playoffs by the Carolina Hurricanes, losing the series 4-0. The Hurricanes won the final game 4-2, with Logan Stankoven scoring the go-ahead goal in the third period. The Senators' season came to an abrupt end with the loss at home on Saturday afternoon. Despite a season with many twists and turns, the team was unable to overcome the Hurricanes' strong play. The sweep leaves the Senators with plenty of off-season question marks, while the Hurricanes move on to the second round of the playoffs. Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark made several big saves, but it was not enough to prevent the loss. The team will now regroup and look to rebuild for next season. The Hurricanes' win marks a dominant performance in the first-round series.

stories.headline: No. 6 UCLA Powers Past No. 25 Washington
stories.summary: The No. 6 UCLA softball team defeated No. 25 Washington 7-2 on Saturday, securing the series win at Husky Softball Stadium in front of a sold-out crowd of 1,963 fans. This victory follows Friday's 7-5 win, where freshman Bri Alejandre hit a go-ahead, two-run home run in the seventh inning. In the middle game of the series, UCLA hit four homers and Taylor Tinsley struck out Alexis DeBoer to escape a bases-loaded jam. The Bruins' series win comes after a previous close match between the teams on December 3, where UCLA won 82-80 with 25 points from Skyy Clark. The recent series saw UCLA's strong performance, with Alejandre's late homer lifting the team to victory in the series opener. UCLA's wins secure their lead in the Big Ten Conference series.

stories.headline: UP triple murder: 3 shot dead after cake-smearing dispute at birthday party inside gym
stories.summary: A dispute over cake-smearing at a birthday party in a gym in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, escalated into a violent clash, leaving three people dead. The altercation began when one of the victims allegedly smeared cake on the face of the birthday boy, Jeetu Saini. Amardeep, Manish Saini, and Akash Saini were shot dead and declared dead upon arrival at the hospital. The primary accused, Jeetu Saini, and several accomplices are at large. Police, including Meerut Range DIG Kalanidhi Naithani, visited the scene to oversee the investigation. The deceased have been identified as Amardeep Saini, Manish Saini, and Akash Saini. The incident is under investigation, with authorities working to apprehend the accused. The violent clash occurred during a birthday celebration, resulting in the tragic loss of three lives.

stories.headline: AAP to move Rajya Sabha chair, President against Raghav Chadha-led rebel MPs who joined BJP
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has petitioned Rajya Sabha Chairman, Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar, to terminate the membership of seven MPs who left the party to join the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). AAP leader Sanjay Singh submitted the petition seeking disqualification of the seven MPs. The move comes after the MPs, led by Raghav Chadha, defected to the BJP, weakening the AAP ahead of the Punjab polls. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has also sought President Droupadi Murmu's intervention in the matter. The AAP has cited the anti-defection law to seek the disqualification of the rebel MPs, who had recently joined the BJP, causing a significant setback to the party. The petition is currently with the Rajya Sabha Chairman for consideration.

stories.headline: On the run for 26 years: Delhi police arrest life convict in Ghaziabad, lived as YouTuber
stories.summary: Delhi police have arrested Salim Khan, a 54-year-old life convict, in Ghaziabad after he evaded capture for 26 years. Khan, who assumed the alias "Salim Wastik," was living openly in Loni, Ghaziabad, and ran a YouTube channel with over 63,000 subscribers. He was convicted in 1995 for the kidnapping and murder of 13-year-old Sandeep Bansal in Northeast Delhi's Gokalpuri area. The arrest has brought back painful memories for the victim's parents, who still reside in the same area where their son was killed. Khan's arrest is a significant development, and the case has been reopened, providing some closure for the family after three decades. The Delhi police's efforts have finally led to the apprehension of the fugitive, who had been living a seemingly normal life under an assumed identity.

stories.headline: Rs 289 crore, 25 acres, 15 students: Inside India's 'ghost campus' Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology in Greater Noida
stories.summary: The Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on March 9, 2019. Built at a cost of Rs 289 crore, the institute spans 25 acres and features a four-storey building with modern amenities, including an auditorium, open-air theatre, and archaeological museum. Despite its grand infrastructure, the institute is currently operating with only 15 students. The institute was established to be a premier centre for training and research in archaeology, but its current state reveals a stark contrast between its facilities and operational capacity. The institute's building is equipped with the latest technologies and has a 3-star ultra-modern green rating, but its underutilization has raised questions about its effectiveness in achieving its intended purpose. The institute is located in Knowledge Park II area, adjacent to Galgotias College of Engineering and Technology.

stories.headline: Japan inflation cools demand for vending machine drinks
stories.summary: Japan's vending machines, a cultural mainstay with over 5.5 million nationwide, are facing decreased demand for drinks due to rising inflation. With one vending machine for every 23 people, the highest ratio in the world, operators are being forced to reassess their business strategies. The rapid pace of inflation is cooling demand for vending machine drinks, prompting a rethink of the industry. Vending machines can be found in various locations, including post offices, parks, stations, and even the summit of Mount Fuji. As inflation weakens demand, operators must adapt to the changing market conditions and find new ways to remain viable in a country where vending machines are an integral part of daily life. The shift in consumer behavior is a significant challenge for the industry, which has long been a staple of Japanese culture.

stories.headline: Consumers to receive $10m cashback boost from DBS amid cost pressures
stories.summary: DBS Bank will provide $10 million in cashback redemptions to customers between August and December. The initiative aims to help Singaporeans offset the cost of everyday items like groceries and food amid rising expenses. The bank's decision comes amid prolonged uncertainty and escalating costs. The $10 million cashback boost is part of DBS' support for customers facing increasing financial pressures. This move is designed to alleviate the burden of higher prices for essential items. DBS announced the initiative on April 25, highlighting its commitment to helping customers manage their finances during challenging times. The cashback redemptions will be available to customers through DBS' platforms, providing them with some relief from the rising cost of living.

stories.headline: Better Growth Investment to Buy With $500: Ethereum vs. Strategy
stories.summary: Ethereum is considered a better investment option for $500 compared to Strategy. Strategy's performance is closely tied to Bitcoin's price and its ability to secure favorable capital funding, limiting its potential for growth. In contrast, Ethereum offers more diverse investment opportunities. Recently, Strategy purchased an additional 1,955 BTC for approximately $217.4 million, bringing its total holdings to 638,460 BTC at an average price of $111,196 per bitcoin. This significant investment in Bitcoin underscores Strategy's reliance on the cryptocurrency's performance. As a result, investors looking to allocate $500 for growth may find Ethereum to be a more attractive option due to its broader potential for expansion and development. Ethereum's growth prospects appear more promising compared to Strategy's Bitcoin-centric approach.

stories.headline: Want Decades of Passive Income? 4 Energy Stocks to Buy Right Now
stories.summary: High oil prices driven by reduced global oil and natural gas supplies due to the Middle East conflict have driven energy stocks higher. For long-term passive income, The Motley Fool recommends four energy stocks: Enterprise Products Partners, Enbridge, ExxonMobil, and Chevron. These companies are proven survivors and can provide decades of dividend income. The midstream energy space is a promising area for high-yield stocks with solidly growing passive income. As of March 27, 2026, these stocks are endorsed for their potential to generate long-term income. Morningstar analysts have provided commentary on each company, highlighting their strengths and potential for growth. Investors seeking stable and growing dividend income can consider these energy stocks for their portfolios. Reduced supply and rising prices in the commodity market support the potential for long-term income from these stocks.
